answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Valid agents interlink credentials like a climbing vine of trust, preventing any isolated rogue entity from masquerading as an autonomous peer. To enter the network without such history, each newly spawned clone must stake collateral that scales superlinearly (O(2^n)), imposing exponential capital exhaustion on Sybil swarms. This economic barrier acts as a crystal shield, transforming the attacker's swarm into an unsustainable, economically stranded island.
